solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: the sailor's verb: to sound water is to take its depth with a weighted line
to rumble someone is to see through them, to work them out

annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like noises, and neither is: 'sound' is the sailor's depth-taking verb and 'rumble' is informal British for finding someone out.
annotation.definitionFit: To fathom is both to take a depth and to get to the bottom of someone.

entries.clue: Clay pots I love for dressing (5)

indicatorNotes.pots: to pot is to put something in, as a snooker ball is potted into a pocket

blocks.note: Cassius Clay was the boxer's name before he became Muhammad Ali
taken as printed
love = nil = O

annotation.surface: A potter's kiln of clay pots, and someone declaring their fondness for dressing them up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clay pots' reads as pottery; Clay is the boxer, and 'pots' is the verb that puts IO inside him.
annotation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, served as a dressing or dip.

entries.clue: One rash he had to get treated (7)

indicatorNotes.treated: treated as in processed or worked on, so the letters are changed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A man with a skin rash who had no choice but to see a doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint needing treatment; it is the adjective, reckless.
annotation.definitionFit: A person whose head runs hot acts before thinking, which is what rash means.

blocks.note: the surface wants a cassette or reel; the setter means a tape measure
not audio but the figure such a tape reads off; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: Someone asking about a cassette or reel of recorded audio.
annotation.walkthrough: The tape is a tape measure, not a cassette, and what it records is a measurement.
annotation.definitionFit: A measurement is the reading taken off a measuring tape.

annotation.definitionNote: Crow is one people, AMERINDS the plural; 'say' marks Crow as one example of them

indicatorNotes.represented: re-presented: the letters are presented in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A black bird appearing symbolically in someone's dreams.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird; the Crow are a Native American people of Montana.
annotation.definitionFit: The Crow are one of the indigenous peoples of America, the Amerinds.

indicatorNotes.adjusted: the letters are altered into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
anagram fodder, 11 letters, joined to the first part by 'with'

annotation.surface: A pharmacist fine-tuning a dosage after calibrating the equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is careful pharmacy, which fits the drug neatly; the two fodder words together make exactly fifteen letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An anabolic steroid is a drug that builds muscle tissue.

entries.clue: Aim of those ahead of foe? (3)

indicatorNotes.those ahead of: the letters that stand just ahead of each of F, O and E in the alphabet

blocks.note: E comes before F, N before O, D before E

annotation.surface: Asking what troops in the front line intend against the enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those ahead' look like soldiers advancing; they are the alphabet's letters just before F, O and E.
annotation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'.

blocks.note: the surface wants British suspenders, the straps holding up stockings; the setter means anything that hangs
not slipping clothing but hanging things of ice that drop in a thaw

annotation.surface: Stockings losing their support on a hot day.
annotation.walkthrough: Suspenders here are simply things that hang (British suspenders hold up stockings, which the surface leans on); icicles hang, and fall when it warms.
annotation.definitionFit: Icicles are suspended from eaves and drop when the temperature climbs.

blocks.note: winning = charming, as in a winning smile
giving up weapons

annotation.surface: Victory achieved by laying down arms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winning' looks like victory; it is the adjective, as in a disarming smile.
annotation.definitionFit: A disarming manner wins people over; disarming is also removing weapons.

blocks.note: the Contras were Nicaraguan rebels of the 1980s
a band is a group

annotation.surface: A rebel group has been outlawed.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Contraband goods are prohibited ones, as an adjective.

entries.clue: This month, in an abbreviated way (4)

blocks.note: taken as printed
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

annotation.surface: Referring to the current month in shorthand.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes the answer itself: inst. is old business-letter shorthand for instant, meaning this month.
annotation.definitionFit: Inst. (instant) in formal letters means of the current month.

entries.clue: Suddenly slowing ceremony, maniac takes over (8)

indicatorNotes.takes: the maniac takes on over as a following piece

blocks.note: a rite is a ceremony
a nut is a maniac
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

annotation.surface: A ceremony grinds to a halt when a lunatic seizes control.
annotation.walkthrough: Ritenuto is an Italian musical direction meaning held back at once, unlike the gradual ritardando.
annotation.definitionFit: Ritenuto marks an immediate slowing of tempo in music.

indicatorNotes.Cut by: the blood is split open with aluminium placed in the cut

blocks.note: gore is spilt blood
Al is the chemical symbol

annotation.surface: A cut from an aluminium edge leaves blood all over the place.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a messy injury; 'everywhere' is loose for galore, in abundance.
annotation.definitionFit: Things galore are in plenty, to be found everywhere.

blocks.note: to ground someone in a subject is to prepare them
done well = done properly

annotation.surface: Someone getting thoroughly ready for a surge of the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising tide' may be read literally, but a groundswell is also a surge of opinion.
annotation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a building wave of feeling, like a rising tide.

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
pud is British slang for pudding, a sweet course

annotation.surface: Describing a vegetable that is little and sugary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective describing the vegetable; it is the noun, a dessert, which the British call pud.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is broad: spud is slang for one particular vegetable, the potato.

entries.clue: Training to get upset girl in bed (9)

indicatorNotes.to get: the training has the next letters put into it
indicatorNotes.in: they go in, between P and E

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
to ail is to trouble or upset
a lass is a girl

annotation.surface: A distressed girl being coaxed into bed after exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram indicator, but it is AIL, the verb meaning to trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: A paillasse is a straw-filled mattress.

entries.clue: Team bagging rubbish over in newspaper office (10)

indicatorNotes.bagging: the team puts the rubbish in its bag
indicatorNotes.over: turns the whole thing over, back to front

blocks.note: a side is a team
rot is nonsense
in = fashionable = hip

annotation.surface: A crew carrying off rubbish bags left all over a newspaper's offices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office' here means a post held, not a room, and 'in' is the adjective meaning fashionable, not a placing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Office in the sense of a position held: the post of running a paper.

entries.clue: The main available period for tourism (4,6)

blocks.note: the main is poetic for the open sea, the high seas
on = available, as in 'on offer'

annotation.surface: The chief time of year when holidays can be booked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The main' reads as 'the chief'; it is the old word for the ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: High season is the busiest period of the tourist year.

blocks.note: to heave is to lift with effort
North and South are partners at bridge

annotation.surface: Someone complaining how hard it is to lift a pair of partners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise, as 'Heavens!' is.
annotation.definitionFit: 'My!' and 'Heavens!' are the same surprised exclamation.

blocks.note: the verb: to plead or press earnestly
the verb: to advise or recommend a course

annotation.surface: Pleading with a lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister to be appealed to; it is the verb, to advise.
annotation.definitionFit: To urge is both to plead and to recommend.

entries.clue: Greek hero deviously sly in exploits (7)

indicatorNotes.deviously: the letters take a crooked route
indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled letters sit in the exploits, placed inside that word

blocks.note: anagram of SLY
to exploit is to use

annotation.surface: A cunning Greek warrior getting up to his schemes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Ulysses, the Latin name for Odysseus, was the craftiest of the Greek heroes. 'Exploits' looks like deeds; it is the verb USES.
annotation.definitionFit: Ulysses is the Roman name for Odysseus, hero of the Odyssey.

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a plant is a factory

annotation.surface: A worker in a factory that manufactures plastic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' reads as the material a factory makes; it is the adjective, bendable.
annotation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means pliant, easily shaped.

entries.clue: Appearing in Times, say, is Times writer (8)

annotation.definition: Appearing in Times, say, is Times writer

indicatorNotes.Appearing in: the answer appears inside the words that follow

blocks.note: timES SAY IS Times

annotation.surface: A newspaper columnist's byline in The Times.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an essayist is exactly a writer whose pieces appear in The Times.
annotation.definitionFit: An essayist writes short prose pieces, the kind a newspaper prints.

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, back to front, as a down answer read upward

blocks.note: a loop is a turn

annotation.surface: A cylinder rotating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like the verb for what a cylinder does; it is the noun, loops.
annotation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread or film is wound.

entries.clue: Body in water dissolved in seconds? (4)

indicatorNotes.in seconds: take the second letter of each pair: 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th

blocks.note: dIsSoLvEd

annotation.surface: Asking whether a corpse left in water would dissolve within seconds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Body in water' suggests a corpse and 'dissolved' a chemical process; the body is an island, and 'dissolved' is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A land mass sitting in the sea is a body in water, the geographer's sense of body.

blocks.note: an occupation or calling
a public declaration, as of faith or love

annotation.surface: A notice advertising a vacancy.
annotation.walkthrough: The pair reads as a job advert; the second sense is a declaration, as in a profession of love.
annotation.definitionFit: Profession means both an occupation and an avowal.

blocks.note: British slang for a very awkward task, named after a greedy farm animal
scoff is British slang for eating greedily, like that farm animal

annotation.surface: Food that is hard to wolf down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' could mean to mock; here it is the British informal verb for eating greedily.
annotation.definitionFit: A pig is a hard task, and to pig is to gorge.

blocks.note: a mess is a military dining room
silver-haired, so old

annotation.surface: Someone got in touch with the dining hall about the silverware.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silver' looks like cutlery or AG; here it means grey with age.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sending someone a text or email is getting in contact.

entries.clue: Stone left in position to finish (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the stone and left go inside the position

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
L = left
the lay of the land is its position or arrangement

annotation.surface: A curling stone left in place at the end of play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, but it is the abbreviation L.
annotation.definitionFit: Lastly and 'to finish' both introduce a final point.
